title: RW Aurigae — a young variable star
status: measured; no change confirmed by our pre-set rule
plain_result: Its centre overloads SPHEREx's detector, so we measured it from the halo of light around it, a method tested first on 41 ordinary stars of similar brightness. Between the two visits (Sep 2025 and Mar 2026) it looks 48 ± 16% brighter at 0.9 µm and 39 ± 11% at 1.4 µm, but 21 ± 5% fainter at 4.1 µm: not a grey change, bigger in the bluest colours, the pattern our literature notes predicted, before this measurement, if the fading reported in early 2025 had ended between our visits. One band passes 5 times its error in one visit, but the rule we wrote down beforehand needs two, and its own pictures scatter 1.1–3 times more than the ordinary stars' (which widens its errors), so no change is confirmed.

method_note: Halo photometry (annulus 4–7 pixels) chosen and its errors set on comparison stars before RW Aurigae was measured (docs/protocols/E9.md); 4.4–5 µm not used (more saturated than any comparison star). The colour-by-colour errors use the star's own picture scatter, applied after the result (labelled in the results file). RW Aurigae is an unresolved pair 1.5″ apart.
